a:r.a:t: FOXO1 Activates Transcription in Response to Insulin (High Blood Glucose)

p:cNvPr.descr: An image illustrating the mechanism of gene regulation by the transcription factor FOXO1. This image has two boxes on top of each other. The top box is white and entitled cytosol; the bottom box is blue and entitled nucleus. At the top of the cytosol box, there is a yellow line going across, outlined in blue, representing plasma membrane. At the top left is a red circle labeled as insulin, which points to that red circle on a figure that breaks through the plasma membrane and has two blue circular knos at the bottom. These knobs have black lines darting all around them. From there, two black arrows point down to a blue image PKB, which sits on a curved arrow pointing right. That arrow points from a tan oval FOXO1 and points to another tan oval FOXO1. The second tan oval FOXO1 has a curved arrow at the bottom pointing back (left) to the first tan oval FOXO1. It also has a shorter arrow pointing off to P1. Below the curved arrow pointing left is phosphoprotein phosphatase written in blue. To the right of the second tan oval FOXO1 is a black P in a red circle. At the top right of the second tan oval FOXO1 is arrow pointing up and right entitled ubiquitin, which points to another arrow above that entitled proteasome. This arrow points to broekn up tan pieces. The first tan oval FOXO1 also has reversible arrows pointing through the nucleus box to another tan oval FOXO1. Below that is a blue DNA string going horizontally right. A small arrow points up and right from the DNA string to a wavy green mRNA arrow, which also has an arrow pointing to PEP carboxykinase glucose 6-phosphatase.
